title: In repos/development-vessel/src/resolvers/gap-to-feature.ts, make a NAMED change site resolve to a line so the drafter i
description:
In repos/development-vessel/src/resolvers/gap-to-feature.ts, make a NAMED change site resolve to a line so the drafter is grounded at the edit site instead of the top of the file.

THE DEFECT (measured): the grounding window is chosen from startLine. startLine comes from a match that requires DIGITS after the colon, so an edit_site like repos/activity-api/src/routes/activities.ts:/conservation-audit yields startLine 0. The existing region-to-line fallback cannot help because meta.region is null for these gaps. The window therefore becomes lines 1 to 40 of an 11645 line file and the MATCH ANCHOR becomes an import statement about 5800 lines away from the real edit site, so every draft invents the target text and is refused with anchor_not_found or DRIFT-REFUSED. Nothing is logged when meta.region is empty, so the fallback is silent.

THE CHANGE. Edit exactly this line, which occurs EXACTLY ONCE in the file (copy it verbatim as your anchor):
            const region = String(meta.region ?? "").trim();

Replace it so that when meta.region is empty, region falls back to the NAME part of the change site: take the first whitespace-separated token of siteStr, take the text after its first colon, drop a single leading forward slash if present, and use empty string when that text is purely numeric (a line number is already handled above). Keep meta.region as the preferred value. This reuses the region-to-line grep and logging that already follows, so a named site will now ground the window and emit the existing log line.

CONSTRAINTS. One edit, one line, in place. Do not add a helper function and do not change any other line. Do not use regular expression literals or any escape characters; use plain string methods such as trim, split, indexOf, slice and startsWith, and test for numeric text with Number and Number.isNaN. The result must typecheck and must keep the surrounding code unchanged.
